description: pinout trap, pins by FUNCTION: Q1 is declared {E: GND, B: OUT, C: LED_A} and bound to the BC547 record (pads 1=C 2=B 3=E) instead of 2N3904 (1=E 2=B 3=C). The registry derives pad numbers from the record, so the netlist is renumbered consistently (GND lands on pad 3, not pad 1) and there is nothing left to catch
note: CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION (negative control, must stay CLEAN). Supersedes the M-libpin-swap gap for registry parts declared by function: the wrong-library-pinout class cannot occur because no pad number is typed. What stays possible is a wrong FUNCTION in netlist.py (e.g. {C: GND}): a design mistake for the P2 role/voltage checks, not a library mistake. To see the renumbering: run with --keep and compare Q1.pins for 2n3904-to92 (1=GND,2=OUT,3=LED_A) with bc547-to92 (3=GND,2=OUT,1=LED_A).
